subject: french
title: Stamp 3: Register and Intertextuality
welcome_lead: Stamp your understanding of register and intertextual references.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on registre, intertextualite, and stylistic levels.

concepts.def: Register: the tonal or stylistic mode of a text (tragic, comic, satirical, lyric).
Elevated, formal register used in literary or formal contexts.
Colloquial register reflecting informal everyday speech.
Intertextuality: relationships between texts through allusion, quotation, or pastiche.
Pastiche: imitation of another author's style, sometimes affectionately.
Parody: comic imitation that mocks the original.

walkthroughs.body_html: Vocabulary signals register. Aller (neutral), se rendre a (soutenu), foncer (familier). Sentence length, syntax, and figures of speech all contribute to the overall register.
When a modern novel quotes Racine, the reader's recognition adds layers of meaning. Julia Kristeva coined the term intertextualite in 1966, drawing on Bakhtin's dialogism.
Proust wrote pastiches imitating Flaubert, Balzac, etc., affectionately. Parody is mocking: a parody of a romantic poem exaggerates its conventions to ridicule them.

numericals.q: In what year did Kristeva introduce the term 'intertextualite'?
